title: pairwise-sanity-sweep-runbook-2026
body:
Purpose
This runbook describes a compact, automatable "sanity sweep" for reranking evaluation bundles used in model onboarding. The goal is to catch obvious regressions, dataset format issues, and slice-level failures before a full human-in-the-loop audit. Use this for every candidate model and for PRs that touch sampling, labeling, or metric code.

Scope
- Small-to-medium sized pairwise/choice bundles (1k-25k pairwise judgments)
- Automated NDCG smoke tests + slice-level stability checks
- Quick labeler/agreement and data-format validation
- Perturbation experiments (synthetic) to detect brittleness

Inputs (expected)
- pairwise.csv: CSV with columns: query_id, candidate_a_id, candidate_b_id, winner (a|b|tie), annotator_id, timestamp, batch_id
- candidates.csv: candidate_id, doc_score, length_tokens, source_bucket
- queries.csv: query_id, text, query_type, user_cohort
- baseline_metrics.json (optional): previous ndcg@k by slice for regression comparison

Outputs
- sanity_report.json (summary of gates and pass/fail)
- ndcg_table.csv: global and per-slice ndcg@1/3/5 with 95% CI
- agreement_summary.csv: per-annotator and pair-level agreement rates
- quick_plots.tar.gz (small pngs: ndcg_by_slice, agreement_hist, perturbation_delta)

Pre-checks (format + basic invariants)
1) Required columns present and non-empty for first 1k rows. Fail early if missing.
2) No duplicate identical pair rows (same query_id and same unordered pair). If duplicates exist, report and dedupe by latest timestamp.
3) Winner values limited to {a,b,tie}. Anything else = invalid.
4) Candidate IDs referenced in pairwise.csv must exist in candidates.csv. Report orphan IDs.

Sampling rules for the sweep
- If bundle > 25k pairs, sample a stratified 5k subset: stratify by query_type and source_bucket.
- Ensure minimum 50 pairs per major slice (if available) by upsampling from that slice; log when below threshold.

Labeler / annotation QC checks
- Per-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's alpha on pairwise converted to ordinal): flag annotators with alpha < 0.2 for review.
- Pairwise majority consistency: for each pair across N annotators, compute majority winner and record disagreement fraction. If disagreement fraction > 0.35 for >10% of pairs, mark bundle for human review.
- Time-per-judgment median check: median < 1s likely bot/automation; > 30s per judgment suggests confusing instructions.

Converting pairwise to relevance scores (two supported heuristics)
1) Win-rate scoring (preferred for sanity sweep): for each candidate within a query, score = wins / (wins + losses). Ties count as 0.5 win for both. Normalize to [0,1].
2) Bradley-Terry fit (optional): fit a BT model per query group when you need rankings that respect pairwise transitivity; slower. Use only on >= 300 pairs per query.
Note: avoid forcing integer relevance labels for the sweep — treat as graded gains when computing NDCG.

NDCG calculation details
- Use ndcg@1,3,5. Gains = raw score (0-1) converted by gain = 2^{score} - 1 when comparing to previous pipelines for compatibility; for quick checks linear gains (gain = score) are acceptable but must be documented.
- Discount = log2(rank + 1).
- When ties occur at cutoff, compute expected ndcg by averaging across all tie-break permutations (deterministic small-sample approximation).
- Bootstrapped 95% CI: 1k resamples by default for the sweep; compute percentile CI. For heavy-duty runs switch to 10k.

Regression gates (sweep-level thresholds)
- Global ndcg@5 drop vs baseline: fail if drop > 0.008 absolute AND p-value < 0.05 from bootstrap difference.
- Slice-level: fail if any slice with >100 queries shows ndcg@5 drop > 0.015 absolute.
- Agreement regression: average annotator alpha drop > 0.05 triggers human review.
- Any parsing/orphan ID errors = immediate fail.

Slice definitions (recommended for sweep)
- cold_start: queries with user_cohort == "new_user" OR queries with zero historical clicks
- long_query: len(text.split()) >= 8
- commercial_intent: query_type in {"purchase","pricing","product"}
- truncation_sensitive: candidate length_tokens > 512 and baseline_doc_score high (>0.7)
- multi_doc: queries where candidates.csv indicates source_bucket == "multi_doc"
Note: slices are additive; a query may be in multiple slices. Report intersections for interpretation.

Perturbation experiments (automated, cheap)
1) Paraphrase sweep: generate 2 paraphrases per query (use lightweight paraphraser) and recompute ndcg delta. Significant sensitivity (median |delta| > 0.02) indicates lexical brittleness.
2) Prefix/noise injection: add token noise at start of query ("asdf") for 5% of test queries to catch models that overfit signal position.
3) Truncation: truncate context to 128 tokens for candidates > 512 tokens and measure drop.
4) Relevance inversion synthetic check: swap winners for 2% of high-confidence pairs and expect ndcg to drop > 0.05; if it doesn't, metric pipeline may be broken.

Automation commands (example)
- Run full sweep: python scripts/sanity_sweep.py --pairs pairwise.csv --candidates candidates.csv --queries queries.csv --out-dir /tmp/sweep_out --bootstrap 1000
- Generate quick report only: python scripts/quick_ndcg.py --pairs pairwise.csv --k 5 --bootstrap 500
- Convert to wins: python scripts/pairwise_to_scores.py --input pairwise.csv --output scores.csv --method winrate

Expected CSV formats (examples)
- pairwise.csv header: query_id,candidate_a_id,candidate_b_id,winner,annotator_id,timestamp,batch_id
- scores.csv header: query_id,candidate_id,score,num_pairs,win_rate

Quick interpretation examples
- Output snippet: ndcg@5 global: 0.842 (95% CI 0.835-0.849). Baseline: 0.849 -> delta = -0.007 (p=0.12) => pass gate (small drop, not significant).
- Slice: cold_start ndcg@5 = 0.701 (95% CI 0.680-0.722). Baseline slice = 0.718 -> delta = -0.017 (p=0.03) => FAIL (slice-level regression).

Troubleshooting checklist
- If bootstrapped CI is unreasonably wide (>0.05 width): check sample size, stratify differently, increase resamples.
- If converted scores look all-zero or 1.0: inspect pairwise duplicates and tie handling; check for annotator bias (all same annotator).
- If perturbation delta is zero across experiments: verify that perturbation pipeline is applying changes (sampling bug) and that candidate IDs are stable across transforms.

Escalation and next steps on fail:
1) Re-run sweep on full dataset (no sampling) to confirm.
2) If confirmed, run human-in-the-loop slice audit: select 200 pairs from failing slice, send to senior labelers with adjudication.
3) If still failing, open a regression incident and notify applied-ml and serving-runtime with summary + artifacts.

Change log
- 2026-01-12: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2026-02-15: added perturbation experiments and regression gates (Hannah)

Notes / open questions
- Should win-rate be default tie-breaker for final reports? (pros: simple; cons: ignores transitivity). Will propose to eval owners.
- Consider adding a small reproducible Jupyter notebook for visualizing per-query pair graphs for cases with high disagreement.

Contact
- Primary: Aisha Mehta (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Applied ML lead: Luis Garcia

End of runbook
